raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Allow disaggregated prefill servers to reuse KV cached in LMCache.

## Modifications

Enable LMCache on prefill servers and wait for asynchronous KV loads before sending cached prefixes to decode, including when overlap is disabled. Decode-side LMCache remains unsupported.

Add an engine-driven shared-memory (SHM) configuration, a reuse benchmark, and configuration/lifecycle/end-to-end tests. Includes the store-ordering fix in #47558.

## Accuracy Tests

On MI355X / ROCm 10, Qwen3-8B TP=2 and two-node Qwen3-0.6B TP=1 passed strict 16-token comparisons against a no-LMCache baseline, covering cold requests, external hits, cache-salt isolation and both-server restarts. Warm and restarted cross-node requests reused 1024 external tokens with zero device hits. Tests used SHM and Mooncake TCP (`MC_FORCE_TCP=1`).

Combined integration a1477798 passed 459 tests and 262 subtests. Default Mooncake HIP TP=2 and LMCache-driven IPC TP=2 remain unresolved on this stack. Hosted CI is pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

At a5b77ce1, Qwen3-0.6B TP=1, input/output 3073/64, concurrency 8: inline versus SHM measured 83.82 versus 610.47 output tokens/s over 512 requests with exact output equality. Both used non-lazy 16 GiB L1 pools; throughput excludes cache priming and flushes.

 For full LMCache config options see https://docs.lmcache.ai/api_reference/configurations.html.
+
+## Engine-driven shared-memory transfers
+
+Engine-driven transfers keep GPU copies in the SGLang worker. With a shared
+host IPC namespace, a named SHM pool lets the worker copy KV directly to/from
+the daemon's CPU buffers, avoiding bulk inline message payloads. The daemon
+and SGLang processes must see the same `/dev/shm`, even when they run in
+different containers. The pool must use non-lazy allocation.
+
+Start the daemon:
+
+```bash
+lmcache server \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5556 \
+  --l1-size-gb 16 --no-l1-use-lazy \
+  --chunk-size 256 --eviction-policy LRU \
+  --supported-transfer-mode engine_driven \
+  --shm-name sglang_kv_pool
+```
+
+Connect SGLang using `example_config_mp_engine_driven.yaml` from this directory:
+
+```bash
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+  --enable-lmcache \
+  --lmcache-config-file example_config_mp_engine_driven.yaml \
+  --enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend triton \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.1 --max-total-tokens 65536 --context-length 4096 \
+  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
+```
+
+Confirm the SGLang startup log reports `Creating EngineDrivenContextShm`.
+`Creating EngineDrivenContextInline` means the shared-memory path was not
+selected. Omitting the daemon's `--shm-name` selects inline engine-driven
+transfers with the same client configuration.
+
+Validation used MI355X, ROCm 10, PyTorch 2.11 and LMCache
+[a005bb1](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/tree/a005bb19715d1e7a32372e6c4c850b73366cbcc5).
+Engine-driven SHM preserved the restored 1024-token prefix byte-for-byte
+across 56 KV tensors on each of two TP ranks. Rerun the checks when changing
+the engine or driver versions.
+
+### Measure external reuse
+
+From the repository root, benchmark a running isolated server:
+
+```bash
+python test/manual/mem_cache/benchmark_lmcache_reuse.py \
+  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+  --input-len 3073 --output-len 64 --concurrency 8 \
+  --warmup 4 --waves 16 --output reuse.json
+```
+
+The benchmark uses separate cache salts, primes external KV, and flushes GPU
+KV between waves. It checks output equality and full external-only hits. The
+server's GPU token pool must fit the concurrent requests; the example above
+uses 65536 tokens. Its wave throughput includes prefill and decode but excludes
+priming and cache flushes, so it is not steady-state production throughput.
+Use `--prefill-url` with a PD router to flush the prefill server. For a separate
+recomputation run, use `--expected-storage-hit 0` against a server that bypasses
+external loading, keeping the model and other serving settings fixed.
+
+On the validated stack, two runs per transport with the workload above gave
+83.82 output tokens/s for inline transfers and 610.47 output tokens/s for SHM,
+aggregated over measured wave durations. Median TTFT was 5369.17 ms and
+130.56 ms respectively. All 512 measured requests returned identical tokens
+across transports, with 3072 external hit tokens and zero device hits each.
+Both paths used the same non-lazy 16 GiB L1 pool, ordered inline/SHM/SHM/inline.
+Measurements used revision `a5b77ce1`, with stores ordered after the producer.
+These results compare engine-driven transports on this workload; they do not
+establish gains over IPC transfers or another serving engine.
+
+## Disaggregated prefill
+
+Enable LMCache on the prefill server with `--disaggregation-mode prefill`
+alongside the usual PD transfer configuration. The prefill server retrieves
+reusable KV from LMCache and sends it to decode through the configured PD
+backend. Run the decode server without `--enable-lmcache`.
+
+The standalone LMCache service can retain KV across prefill server restarts.
+Keep the model, KV dtype, tensor-parallel layout, and LMCache configuration
+consistent between runs. Early prefix sends wait for asynchronous LMCache
+loads on the forward stream, including with `--disable-overlap-schedule`.
+
+PD decode, DP attention, DCP, and speculative decoding remain unsupported
+with `--enable-lmcache`.
+
+For strict output comparisons, enable `--enable-deterministic-inference` with
+a supported attention backend on both PD servers. Prefix reuse changes the
+prefill computation shape; non-deterministic kernels can produce different
+tokens even when the restored prefix KV is byte-identical.
+
+### Validate PD reuse
+
+With SGLang, LMCache, and the PD transfer backend installed in the same active
+Python environment, run the manual end-to-end test from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+LMCACHE_MP_TRANSFER_MODE=engine_driven \
+  python test/manual/mem_cache/test_disaggregation_lmcache.py -v
+```
+
+The test starts its own daemon and prefill/decode servers. It compares greedy
+tokens against a no-LMCache baseline, verifies external hits after a local
+cache flush and both engine restarts, and checks cache-salt isolation.
+It requires two GPUs, or four with `SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_TP_SIZE=2`.
+Set `LMCACHE_MP_TRANSFER_MODE=lmcache_driven` to exercise IPC transfers and
+`SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_DISABLE_OVERLAP=1` to disable overlap scheduling.
+Set `SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_SHM=1` with engine-driven mode to validate the named
+SHM pool. The test creates its own unique pool name.
+The default model is `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`; override it with
+`SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_MODEL`. `SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_BASE_PORT` (default `31500`)
+reserves the next seven ports for this test. This is a functional test, not a
+latency or throughput benchmark.
+
+On the tested MI355X / ROCm 10 stack, TP=2 passed this test with engine-driven
+LMCache transfers and `MC_FORCE_TCP=1` for Mooncake. Named SHM also passed
+with Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-8B, including both engine restarts and strict
+16-token output parity. These are functional smoke tests rather than a model
+accuracy benchmark. The default same-host
+Mooncake HIP path failed cold-request token parity, and TP=2 LMCache-driven
+IPC retrieval faulted even in colocated SGLang. These paths need separate
+validation; the TCP result does not establish their correctness or RDMA
+performance.

+"""Measure external KV reuse on an isolated, already running SGLang server.
+
+The benchmark flushes the engine's GPU cache between request waves. For PD,
+send generation through the router and set --prefill-url to the prefill server.
+Enable deterministic inference when checking cold/warm output equality.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import math
+import statistics
+import time
+import uuid
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import requests
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+
+def generate(base_url, tokens, salt, output_len):
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    first_token = None
+    result = None
+    with requests.post(
+        base_url + "/generate",
+        json={
+            "input_ids": tokens,
+            "cache_salt": salt,
+            "stream": True,
+            "sampling_params": {
+                "temperature": 0,
+                "max_new_tokens": output_len,
+                "ignore_eos": True,
+            },
+        },
+        stream=True,
+        timeout=180,
+    ) as response:
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        for line in response.iter_lines(chunk_size=1, decode_unicode=True):
+            if not line.startswith("data: ") or line == "data: [DONE]":
+                continue
+            result = json.loads(line[6:])
+            if first_token is None and result.get("output_ids"):
+                first_token = time.perf_counter()
+    if first_token is None or result is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("Server returned no streamed tokens")
+    if len(result["output_ids"]) != output_len:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Incomplete generation: {result}")
+    details = result["meta_info"].get("cached_tokens_details") or {}
+    return {
+        "ttft_ms": (first_token - start) * 1000,
+        "elapsed_ms": (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000,
+        "storage_hits": details.get("storage", 0),
+        "device_hits": details.get("device", 0),
+        "output_ids": result["output_ids"],
+    }
+
+
+def benchmark(args):
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
+    filler = tokenizer.encode("Berlin is the capital of Germany. " * args.input_len)
+    question = tokenizer.encode(
+        "\nWhat is the capital of Germany?\nAnswer:", add_special_tokens=False
+    )
+    tokens = filler[: args.input_len - len(question)] + question
+    if len(tokens) != args.input_len:
+        raise ValueError("Input length is shorter than the benchmark question")
+    expected_hit = (len(tokens) - 1) // args.chunk_size * args.chunk_size
+    if args.expected_storage_hit is not None:
+        expected_hit = args.expected_storage_hit
+    elif expected_hit == 0:
+        raise ValueError("Input length must extend beyond one cache chunk")
+    base_url = args.base_url.rstrip("/")
+    flush_url = (args.prefill_url or args.base_url).rstrip("/") + "/flush_cache"
+    prefix = f"reuse-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
+    salts = [f"{prefix}-{index}" for index in range(args.concurrency)]
+    records = []
+    wave_seconds = []
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.concurrency) as pool:
+
+        def wave():
+            return list(
+                pool.map(
+                    lambda salt: generate(base_url, tokens, salt, args.output_len),
+                    salts,
+                )
+            )
+
+        # Salt-separated requests cannot satisfy one another from GPU radix KV.
+        references = [row["output_ids"] for row in wave()]
+        for index in range(args.warmup + args.waves):
+            requests.post(
+                flush_url, params={"timeout": 60}, timeout=90
+            ).raise_for_status()
+            start = time.perf_counter()
+            rows = wave()
+            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+            for slot, (row, reference) in enumerate(zip(rows, references, strict=True)):
+                if row["output_ids"] != reference:
+                    raise RuntimeError(f"Output mismatch in wave {index}, slot {slot}")
+                if row["device_hits"] != 0 or row["storage_hits"] != expected_hit:
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"Expected {expected_hit} storage hits and zero device hits: {row}"
+                    )
+                if index >= args.warmup:
+                    records.append(dict(row, wave=index - args.warmup, slot=slot))
+            if index >= args.warmup:
+                wave_seconds.append(elapsed)
+    ttft = sorted(row["ttft_ms"] for row in records)
+    summary = {
+        "requests": len(records),
+        "ttft_median_ms": statistics.median(ttft),
+        "ttft_p95_ms": ttft[math.ceil(0.95 * len(ttft)) - 1],
+        "elapsed_mean_ms": statistics.mean(row["elapsed_ms"] for row in records),
+        "wave_requests_per_second": len(records) / sum(wave_seconds),
+        "wave_output_tokens_per_second": len(records)
+        * args.output_len
+        / sum(wave_seconds),
+    }
+    report = {
+        "model": args.model,
+        "input_len": args.input_len,
+        "output_len": args.output_len,
+        "chunk_size": args.chunk_size,
+        "concurrency": args.concurrency,
+        "warmup_waves": args.warmup,
+        "measured_waves": args.waves,
+        "expected_storage_hit": expected_hit,
+        "summary": summary,
+        "wave_seconds": wave_seconds,
+        "records": records,
+    }
+    if args.output:
+        Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000")
+    parser.add_argument("--prefill-url", help="PD prefill endpoint for GPU-cache flush")
+    parser.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
+    parser.add_argument("--input-len", type=int, default=3073)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-len", type=int, default=64)
+    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=256)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--expected-storage-hit",
+        type=int,
+        help="Expected external hit tokens; default full prefix. Use 0 for recompute comparisons.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=4)
+    parser.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", help="Save raw measurements and summary as JSON")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if (
+        min(
+            args.input_len,
+            args.output_len,
+            args.chunk_size,
+            args.concurrency,
+            args.waves,
+        )
+        <= 0
+    ):
+        parser.error("Lengths, chunk size, concurrency and waves must be positive")
+    if args.warmup < 0:
+        parser.error("Warmup waves must be non-negative")
+    if args.expected_storage_hit is not None and args.expected_storage_hit < 0:
+        parser.error("Expected storage hit must be non-negative")
+    benchmark(args)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -0,0 +1,258 @@
+"""External KV reuse on PD prefill with an independent LMCache daemon.
+
+Requires LMCache, a PD transfer backend and two GPUs (four with TP=2).
+Run with an activated environment so the daemon and servers use the same Python.
+"""
+
+import os
+import socket
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+import unittest
+import uuid
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import requests
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+    popen_launch_pd_server,
+    terminate_and_kill_process_tree,
+)
+from sglang.utils import wait_for_http_ready
+
+
+class TestDisaggregationLMCache(unittest.TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.tp_size = int(os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_TP_SIZE", "1"))
+        if torch.cuda.device_count() < 2 * cls.tp_size:
+            raise unittest.SkipTest(f"Requires {2 * cls.tp_size} GPUs")
+        cls.model = os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_MODEL", "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
+        cls.transfer_mode = os.environ.get("LMCACHE_MP_TRANSFER_MODE", "engine_driven")
+        cls.use_shm = os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_SHM") == "1"
+        if cls.use_shm and cls.transfer_mode != "engine_driven":
+            raise ValueError("SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_SHM requires engine_driven transfers")
+        base_port = int(os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_BASE_PORT", "31500"))
+        cls.ports = dict(
+            prefill=base_port + 1,
+            decode=base_port + 2,
+            bootstrap=base_port + 3,
+            cache=base_port + 4,
+            cache_http=base_port + 7,
+        )
+        cls.urls = {
+            role: f"http://127.0.0.1:{cls.ports[role]}"
+            for role in ("prefill", "decode")
+        }
+        cls.nccl_ports = [base_port + 5, base_port + 6]
+        cls.processes = {}
+        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="sglang-lmcache-pd-")
+        cls.addClassCleanup(directory.cleanup)
+        cls.addClassCleanup(cls._stop_all)
+        cls.config_path = Path(directory.name) / "mp.yaml"
+        cls.config_path.write_text(
+            f"mp_host: 127.0.0.1\nmp_port: {cls.ports['cache']}\n"
+            f"extra_config:\n  lmcache.mp.mp_transfer_mode: {cls.transfer_mode}\n"
+        )
+        for port in [*cls.ports.values(), *cls.nccl_ports]:
+            with socket.socket() as probe:
+                probe.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
+                probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
+        # Each invocation owns a fresh daemon, so cold misses and persistence
+        # across engine restarts cannot be satisfied by a previous test run.
+        cache_command = [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "lmcache.cli.main",
+            "server",
+            "--host",
+            "127.0.0.1",
+            "--port",
+            str(cls.ports["cache"]),
+            "--l1-size-gb",
+            "1",
+            "--http-port",
+            str(cls.ports["cache_http"]),
+            "--chunk-size",
+            "256",
+            "--eviction-policy",
+            "LRU",
+            "--supported-transfer-mode",
+            cls.transfer_mode,
+        ]
+        if cls.use_shm:
+            cache_command += [
+                "--no-l1-use-lazy",
+                "--shm-name",
+                f"sglang_kv_test_{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+            ]
+        cls.processes["cache"] = subprocess.Popen(cache_command)
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            if cls.processes["cache"].poll() is not None:
+                raise RuntimeError("LMCache daemon exited during startup")
+            try:
+                with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", cls.ports["cache"]), 1):
+                    break
+            except OSError:
+                time.sleep(0.1)
+        else:
+            raise TimeoutError("LMCache daemon did not start")
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _stop(cls, name):
+        process = cls.processes.pop(name, None)
+        if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
+            terminate_and_kill_process_tree(process)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _stop_all(cls):
+        cls._stop("decode")
+        cls._stop("prefill")
+        cls._stop("cache")
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _start_pair(cls, enable_lmcache):
+        common = [
+            "--tp",
+            str(cls.tp_size),
+            "--attention-backend",
+            "triton",
+            "--enable-deterministic-inference",
+            "--mem-fraction-static",
+            "0.1",
+            "--max-total-tokens",
+            "8192",
+            "--context-length",
+            "4096",
+            "--disable-cuda-graph",
+            "--disaggregation-transfer-backend",
+            os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_PD_DISAGG_BACKEND", "mooncake"),
+            "--disaggregation-bootstrap-port",
+            str(cls.ports["bootstrap"]),
+        ]
+        if os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_LMCACHE_DISABLE_OVERLAP") == "1":
+            common += ["--disable-overlap-schedule"]
+        for index, role in enumerate(("prefill", "decode")):
+            args = common + [
+                "--disaggregation-mode",
+                role,
+                "--base-gpu-id",
+                str(index * cls.tp_size),
+                "--nccl-port",
+                str(cls.nccl_ports[index]),
+            ]
+            if enable_lmcache and role == "prefill":
+                args += [
+                    "--enable-lmcache",
+                    "--lmcache-config-file",
+                    str(cls.config_path),
+                ]
+            cls.processes[role] = popen_launch_pd_server(
+                cls.model,
+                cls.urls[role],
+                timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+                other_args=args,
+                env={"SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX": "1"},
+            )
+            wait_for_http_ready(
+                cls.urls[role] + "/health",
+                timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+                process=cls.processes[role],
+            )
+
+    def _generate(self, cache_salt):
+        payload = {
+            "text": (
+                "Paris is the capital of France. Berlin is the capital of Germany. "
+                * 80
+            )
+            + "\nQuestion: What is the capital of Germany?\nAnswer:",
+            "sampling_params": {
+                "temperature": 0,
+                "max_new_tokens": 16,
+                "ignore_eos": True,
+            },
+            "cache_salt": cache_salt,
+            "return_logprob": True,
+            "bootstrap_host": "127.0.0.1",
+            "bootstrap_port": self.ports["bootstrap"],
+            "bootstrap_room": uuid.uuid4().int % (2**63 - 1),
+        }
+
+        def post(role):
+            body = dict(payload)
+            if role == "prefill":
+                body["sampling_params"] = dict(
+                    payload["sampling_params"], max_new_tokens=1
+                )
+            response = requests.post(
+                self.urls[role] + "/generate", json=body, timeout=180
+            )
+            response.raise_for_status()
+            result = response.json()
+            self.assertNotEqual(result["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"], "abort")
+            return result
+
+        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
+            prefill = pool.submit(post, "prefill")
+            decode = pool.submit(post, "decode")
+            return prefill.result(), decode.result()
+
+    def _flush_local(self):
+        for url in self.urls.values():
+            requests.post(
+                url + "/flush_cache", params={"timeout": 30}, timeout=60
+            ).raise_for_status()
+
+    def test_external_hit_and_engine_restart(self):
+        self._start_pair(enable_lmcache=False)
+        _, baseline = self._generate("shared")
+        reference = baseline["output_ids"]
+        self.assertEqual(len(reference), 16)
+        self._stop("decode")
+        self._stop("prefill")
+        self._start_pair(enable_lmcache=True)
+        cold_prefill, cold_decode = self._generate("shared")
+        self.assertEqual(cold_decode["output_ids"], reference)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (cold_prefill["meta_info"]["cached_tokens_details"] or {}).get(
+                "storage", 0
+            ),
+            0,
+        )
+        self._flush_local()
+        warm_prefill, warm_decode = self._generate("shared")
+        self._assert_external_hit(warm_prefill, warm_decode, reference)
+        self._flush_local()
+        isolated_prefill, isolated_decode = self._generate("isolated")
+        self.assertEqual(isolated_decode["output_ids"], reference)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (isolated_prefill["meta_info"]["cached_tokens_details"] or {}).get(
+                "storage", 0
+            ),
+            0,
+        )
+        self._stop("decode")
+        self._stop("prefill")
+        self._start_pair(enable_lmcache=True)
+        restarted_prefill, restarted_decode = self._generate("shared")
+        self._assert_external_hit(restarted_prefill, restarted_decode, reference)
+
+    def _assert_external_hit(self, prefill, decode, reference):
+        details = prefill["meta_info"]["cached_tokens_details"]
+        self.assertGreater(details["storage"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(details["device"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(decode["output_ids"], reference)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            decode["meta_info"]["cached_tokens_details"]["storage"], details["storage"]
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+    @contextmanager

+    forward.wait_stream.assert_called_once_with(caller)
